Subject: Renewal discussion — need higher monthly commit and higher rate band

Kim / Ben,

Thanks for the check-in. We reviewed our usage Q3 -> Q4 and expect a sustained 2.5-3x uplift in generation volume vs our current commit. A few asks from our side before the renewal: 

- Increase monthly committed tokens from 750M -> 2.25B for the 12-month term.
- Move to the higher usage tier (Tier C) with the reduced per-token rate you have for sustained volume.
- Raise per-route rate limits for our fraud-detection route to 120 requests/s (burst to 250 for 5m) to avoid throttling during promotional spikes.
- Confirm soft-throttle behavior and a canary rollout plan so we don’t see production latency regressions.

We can sign quickly if pricing, soft-throttle, and invoicing align. I’ve looped procurement (procurement@retailnova.com) on next steps and they’ll need a PO template and expected invoice cadence.

Can you send a clear comparison (current vs proposed commit + monthly charge + expected overage behavior) and a short ops runbook for the rollout?

Best,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform — RetailNova

Alex — thanks, this is clear and actionable. Summary of options in attachment (RetailNova_MA_proposal_v3.pdf) but high level here: 

Option A (Recommended): 12mo term, monthly commit -> 2.25B tokens, unit price $0.0008/token (Tier C), includes 25% burst bucket per month and a staged 14-day canary rollout. Soft-throttle threshold: 95th percentile latency target preserved, requests above threshold will be queued up to 30s before soft-failover to fallback variant.

Option B: 6mo term pilot with commit at 1.5B/month, higher per-token rate $0.00095, same burst policy.

We can include a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of first-month committed spend to offset initial ramp costs (valid for signatures before 2028-11-14).

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm preferred option and the PO owner/contact.
- We provide the final SOW and a DocuSign link for signatures.
- Ben will open a provisioning ticket for dedicated burst lanes and rate-limit changes.

I attached a clean proposal and the traffic CSV you sent embedded into our sizing model. Happy to jump on a 30-min call today if helpful.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park

Subject: RetailNova — internal ops & SLA ask (capacity lattice recalibration)

Team — looping you in on RetailNova (RN-2028-Q4-79). External asked to move to 2.25B/month commit and raise route rate limits for fraud route to 120 req/s sustained, burst 250 for 5m windows. Key asks and risks: 

- Provisioning: we need a dedicated soft-burst lane and an ops guardrail to prevent KV-cache exhaustion. Ben, can you estimate ETA for an ops ticket to carve the lane and add the route-specific rate rule?
- SRE: they require a 14-day canary with traffic split 5/95 -> 25/75 -> 100/0. What telemetry and rollback triggers do we surface to the customer? Suggest: token-level cost delta, P95 latency, error-rate spike >0.5%, and request queueing >20s.
- Finance/Legal: Marissa — they want PO-based invoicing and a proposed onboarding credit (10% of month 1). Will that pass? If not, alternate: extended payment terms with first invoiced at net-30 but credit applied.

Proposed internal timeline:
- Today: confirm option A acceptance window (we offered through 11/14).
- 11/03: provision burst lane + set up canary in staging.
- 11/06: begin staged rollout to production (14 days).
- 11/20: full cutover and finalize invoice schedule for December.

I attached the traffic CSV.

Thanks,
Kim

Kim — quick notes after a sync with finance and legal.

Onboarding credit: Finance can approve a 10% onboarding credit applied to the first invoice, conditional on a signed 12-month SOW and revenue recognition rules. We need procurement to confirm PO number before DocuSign.

Billing cadence: RetailNova prefers monthly invoicing, net-30. Legal flagged standard SLA exceptions for burst-provisioning; we should explicitly call out that burst capacity is best-effort and subject to regional capacity caps.

Ops timeline: Ben says carving a route-specific burst lane is 3 business days once ticketed, with a staging validation in 24 hours. Dylan recommends the following canary triggers (happy to use these in the SOW):
- P95 latency > 150ms for more than 10m -> pause rollout
- Error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> rollback
- Queue depth > 50 requests for 10m -> throttle to Tier B variant and notify

I'll draft the amendment language for the SOW (call it "capacity band recalibration — Exhibit A") and share a redline by EOD tomorrow.

—Marissa
